---
title: Get Started with orthoDr
---

orthoDr estimates linear combinations of predictors for modeling a response,
a censored survival outcome, or a personalized dose rule. If your data matrix
$X$ has $p$ predictor columns and you request $d$ directions, the fitted matrix
$B$ has $p$ rows and $d$ columns. The reduced predictors are

$$Z = XB.$$

In R, compute them with `X %*% fit$B`. Each column of `Z` is one weighted
combination of the original predictors. You choose the number of directions
with `ndr`; the fitting functions do not select it automatically.
The package also provides a general optimizer for orthogonality constraints.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source(rprojroot::find_package_root_file("tools", "pkgdown-guide.R"), local = TRUE)
```

## Install and check your version

```{r installation, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat(guide_section("Version and installation"), sep = "\n")
```

## Choose a workflow

| Your task | Start with | Tutorial |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Reduce predictors of a continuous outcome | `orthoDr_reg()` | [Regression](regression.html) |
| Reduce predictors of a censored survival outcome | `orthoDr_surv()` | [Survival](survival.html) |
| Learn a dose rule from features, doses, and rewards | `orthoDr_pdose()` | [Personalized dose finding](personalized-dose.html) |
| Optimize your own objective under $B^T B = I$ | `ortho_optim()` | [General optimizer](general-optimizer.html) |

Start with the regression tutorial for an example of computing reduced
predictors and predicting new responses. Set `keep.data = TRUE` when fitting
a model you will use for prediction. New data must have the same predictor
columns, order, units, and externally applied preprocessing as the training data.

The examples explain the returned values and the numerical `converge` flag.
A direction's sign is arbitrary; with several directions, different bases can
span the same subspace. Compare subspaces or predictions when assessing two fits.

## Download and reproduce the examples

- [Complete getting-started R script](../examples/getting-started.R)
- [Supplemental survival and optimizer R script](../examples/survival-optimizer.R),

Run the complete script to reproduce all four examples. For help matching your
installed version, use `help(package = "orthoDr")`.
